subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@trustai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through TrustAI's inference needs. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned and to capture agreed next steps. If anything below is off, flag it and I'll update.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable latency during peak inference windows (real-time scoring spikes up to ~600 TPS).
- Cost volatility from bursty traffic on shared endpoints; need predictable unit economics for pricing models.
- Data isolation and compliance: customer PII needs to remain within a dedicated environment with strict audit logs.

Current stack and constraints:
- In-house model serving on GCP using mixed GPU fleet (A100 + T4).
- Batch jobs for offline tasks; real-time scoring via a custom FastAPI service.
- Deployments managed by platform team; procurement cycle ~6–8 weeks for new contracts.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Sub-100ms p50 for single-request scoring at baseline load (~200 TPS) and graceful degradation at 600 TPS.
2) Predictable monthly spend with committed capacity option to avoid 3x cost spikes.
3) Dedicated tenancy with KMS integration and audit logs accessible to TrustAI security team.

How Dedicated fits (initial assessment):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) can provide predictable throughput (reserved vGPU slots) and network isolation in a private VPC.
- Autoscaling and burst capacity can be configured with guardrails: we can guarantee baseline reserved TPS and allow controlled burst to a higher tier with rate-limited fallbacks.
- We support KMS/HSM integrations and can provide SOC2 artifacts and an architecture/network diagram for review.

Proposed next steps (agreeing on timing):
1) Technical deep dive (45–60m) — solutions engineer (Rishi) + TrustAI infra team — proposed week of Apr 6. Goal: map request patterns, sequence lengths, KV cache needs, and expected concurrency.
2) Share SOC2 summary + network diagram + mutual action plan (attached).
3) Pricing/contract discussion with procurement once technical fit confirmed — target SOW within 6–8 weeks.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (SOC2 highlights), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP scope + milestones), network_diagram.png (sample Dedicated VPC layout).

Would you be able to confirm availability for the technical deep dive (Apr 6–9) and whether your infra/security leads should be on the call?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom@trustai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@trustai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — recap & next steps

Hey Marissa,

Thanks for the thorough recap — this looks right to me. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

Clarifications:
- Baseline load will be ~150–200 TPS during normal hours, with predictable spikes up to ~600 TPS during batch rollouts (spikes last ~10–20 minutes).
- Typical request payloads are short (<512 tokens) but we have a small subset of longer-context requests (~2–3% at 2k tokens).

Security/compliance asks:
- We will need SOC2 Type II evidence and a network diagram showing VPC connectivity and peering.
- KMS integration is required — keys must be customer-managed.

Operational asks:
- Can Dedicated reserve capacity in a specific region (us-west1) and provide burst capacity that can be pre-authorized? We want to avoid cross-region fallback unless absolutely necessary.
- Procurement timeline: we're aiming to complete procurement by end of May.

Yes — Sofia (cc'd) will be the primary infra contact and should join the technical deep dive. Week of Apr 6 looks good; we prefer Apr 8 at 10am PT if that works for Rishi.

Also, can you include an initial estimate for committed capacity pricing (ballpark per-month) so procurement has something to review? A range is fine.

Appreciate it — Tom

Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering | TrustAI
tom@trustai.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@trustai.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@trustai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Tom / Sofia,

Great — thanks for confirming. Apr 8 at 10am PT works for Rishi and the team; I've penciled it in and sent a calendar invite.

Responses to asks:
- Region: we can reserve Dedicated capacity in us-west1 for you and configure burst rules that require pre-authorization (and we can set a strict policy to avoid automatic cross-region fallback).
- Long-context requests: Rishi will surface expected KV cache behavior and whether quantization/profile adjustments are recommended for the 2k token flows.
- SOC2 & network diagram: attaching SOC2_summary.pdf and network_diagram.png. The SOC2 summary includes where audit logs are stored and retention windows; full SOC2 report can be provided under NDA if needed.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys; we'll include the integration checklist in the tech call.

Pricing: I'll share a ballpark for committed capacity ahead of the tech call. As a rough estimate based on the profile discussed, a reserved pool sized to cover baseline ~200 TPS (with burst window configured to allow short spikes to 600 TPS) would likely fall in the $XXk–$YYk/month range depending on GPU mix and burst allowances. We'll refine after the deep dive.

Next steps action items (owners):
- Marissa: send MAP + SOC2 summary + calendar invite (done).
- TrustAI (Sofia): confirm infra attendees for Apr 8 call.
- Rishi: prepare a short runbook on KV caching, expected throughput per GPU profile, and recommended quantization.
- Vanessa: prepare committed capacity price bands and procurement template to share after the tech call.

Attachments included again for convenience: SOC2_summary.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, network_diagram.png

Looking forward to the call — thanks both.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- I've reviewed the summary and prepared two committed-capacity bands: Standard (baseline 200 TPS reserved, limited burst) and Enterprise (baseline 200 TPS + pre-authorized burst to 600 TPS, dedicated HSM option).
- I'll bring these to the post-tech-call procurement sync. Rishi, please add expected GPU profiles and any constraints on long-context requests to the runbook — that will help us tighten the price bands.
- I'll also pull the procurement clause templates (payment terms, SLA credits) and drop them into the MAP before we send to TrustAI.
